content: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has reported three deaths in infants under 12 months of age in the United States that were linked to the use of cough and cold medications. Medical examiners or coroners determined that these medications were the underlying cause of death. This highlights the importance of clinicians exercising caution when prescribing, and caregivers being cautious when administering, cough and cold medications to children under the age of 2. Guaifenesin works by thinning mucus in the airways, making it easier to cough up and clear the air passages, which helps improve breathing. It is used to relieve coughs caused by colds, bronchitis, and other respiratory infections. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Guaifenesin is available in various forms, including regular and extended-release tablets, capsules, and liquid formulations, all of which are taken orally. Follow the instructions on the package or prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist. Take guaifenesin exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed. Extended-release tablets should not be broken, crushed, or chewed, and extended-release capsules should not be opened; they must be swallowed whole. Drink plenty of fluids while taking this medication unless otherwise directed by your doctor. Guaifenesin is available as a standalone medication or in combination with antihistamines, cough suppressants, and decongestants. Consult your doctor or pharmacist to determine which formulation is most appropriate for your symptoms. If your symptoms persist for more than 7 days, or if you develop a high fever, rash, or persistent headache, contact your doctor. Before taking guaifenesin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to guaifenesin or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking guaifenesin, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose of guaifenesin, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Guaifenesin may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Headache Upset stomach Vomiting Store guaifenesin in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all medical appointments while taking guaifenesin. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Guaifenesin is sold under various brand names, including but not limited to: Brontex® Cheracol® Syrup Diabetic Tussin® EX Mucinex® Robitussin® And many others. Combination products containing guaifenesin include formulations with pseudoephedrine, ephedrine, chlorpheniramine, and phenylephrine, among others. Examples include: Anatuss® LA Bronkaid® Dual Action Caplets® Robitussin® Cold Severe Congestion Liqui-Gels® Sudafed® Non-Drying Sinus Liquid Caps And many others. Consult your doctor or pharmacist to determine the most appropriate product for your condition.
